references.text: Joseph recognized his brothers, but pretended to be a stranger and spoke harshly to them - this is the very event the brothers refer to in v.30.

Joseph accused his brothers of being spies who had come to see the weak points of the land. They defended themselves by saying they were honest men, which directly corresponds to the retelling in v.30.
Joseph was the ruler over the land and sold grain to everyone - he is 'the man, the lord of the land' (אדני הארץ) whom the brothers mention.
Judah refers back to how 'my lord' asked his servants if they had a father or brother, which points back to the harsh treatment from the lord of the land.
Joseph reveals his identity and explains God's plan behind the events, including the harsh treatment the brothers experienced.
Both texts highlight the theme of unjust accusation where the innocent are treated as enemies.
Creates an ironic parallel where the brothers now experience the Egyptian oppression they themselves were subjected to.
